title: Consumer Electronics Ecommerce Benchmarks in 2026
summary: Conversion rate, average order value and bounce rate data for the Consumer Electronics ecommerce category, updated with data through September 2026.
body_markdown:
## Q2’s Pattern Reversed — Consumer Electronics CVR Rebounds in Q3 as AOV Pulls Back


The benchmarks:[1.39% median conversion rate,](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate)[$479 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) . Consumer Electronics ranks eighth in CVR across the 10 published industries. Q3 reversed the pattern from Q2: after posting the steepest CVR decline and the largest AOV gain of any category from Q1 to Q2, Consumer Electronics posted the largest CVR gain (+6.6%) and the steepest same-store AOV decline (−4.4%) of any category from Q2 to Q3.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Consumer Electronics.


The CVR gain comes from a small matched group — 13 stores active in both Q2 and Q3 — so treat it as directional. But it runs 14.1 percentage points ahead of the same quarters in 2025, when CVR fell 7.5%, and the monthly data points the same way: August (1.74%) and September (1.77%) 2026 were the two highest months in the 21-month window. On order value, same-store matched AOV slipped from $403 in Q2 to $386 in Q3 across 46 stores.


One possible reading: the Q2 shift toward fewer, higher-ticket purchases has partly unwound. Conversion recovered in Q3, while the average basket gave back part of its Q2 gain.


In Consumer Electronics, Q3 2026 produced more orders per session at somewhat lower values.


> ***Consumer Electronics went from the steepest CVR decline (−9.5%) and largest AOV gain (+14.4%) in Q2 2026 to the largest CVR gain (+6.6%) and steepest AOV decline (−4.4%) in Q3. Both swings rest on small samples, but the CVR rebound also shows up in the monthly trend.***


## **Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The median Consumer Electronics CVR from January through September 2026 was 1.39%, eighth among the 10 published industries.


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Consumer Electronics cohort: n=20. Small cohort sizes increase the influence of individual stores on the median. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


A 1.39% median CVR is not surprising for a category built on considered purchases. Consumer electronics purchases — whether a new laptop, a set of wireless headphones, or a home theater component — typically involve comparison shopping, specification research, and pricing evaluation before checkout.


Sessions are longer and more deliberate than in repeat-purchase categories, and many visitors leave to continue research before returning to buy.


The P25-to-P75 CVR range is 0.71%–2.01%. The spread is relatively tight, meaning most CE merchants in this cohort cluster within a narrow band.


**The P75 (2.01%) is the lowest top-quartile ceiling of the 10 published industries, reinforcing that even the best-converting CE stores don’t reach the conversion rates common in health, beauty, or food.**


> ***If your Consumer Electronics store is converting above 2.01%, you’re in the top quartile of the category. Below 0.71%, you’re in the bottom quartile. The 1.39% median is the right benchmark — not the cross-industry median of 1.74%.***


## **CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026**


The graph below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Consumer Electronics stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network. Monthly samples are small (12–26 stores), so the direction of the trend is more reliable than any single month.


n=12–26 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Small monthly sample sizes mean individual months can shift on thin data — directional trends are more reliable than specific monthly figures. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Consumer Electronics.


Through 2025, Consumer Electronics CVR ran in a 1.16%–1.60% range without a clear directional trend. Early 2026 moved slightly higher, and Q2 2026 softened to 1.38%–1.39% in May and June after a strong April (1.60%). Then Q3 2026 broke upward: July 1.56%, August 1.74% and September 1.77% — each above the same month of 2025, and the last two the highest readings in the 21-month window.


The bounce rate trend is the clearest signal in the data. Through most of 2025 it ran in the 33%–37% range, with brief rises in July (40.2%) and November–December (40.4%–42.8%). January–March 2026 returned to that range (33.7%–35.5%). Then April 2026 jumped to 43.8%, and bounce rate has held at 42%–44% every month since — about 7 points higher on average than April–September 2025. Through Q2, CVR fell alongside it; in Q3, CVR rose even as bounce rate stayed elevated.


Whether the bounce rate increase reflects a change in traffic quality, shifts in how product pages are presented, or something broader in consumer behavior is hard to determine from aggregate data alone. In Q2 2026, rising bounces and falling CVR moved together; in Q3, the two separated, with CVR recovering while bounce rate held near 44%.


> ***Consumer Electronics bounce rates ran mostly at 33%–37% through 2025. Since April 2026 they have held at 42%–44% — and in Q3, conversion climbed to its highest levels in 21 months anyway.***


## Average Order Value Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Consumer Electronics was $479 across 50 qualifying stores — the second-highest of the 11 categories we track, behind Autos & Vehicles. This data covers full-store Shopify order data, separate from the CVR cohort above.


January–September 2026, n=50 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Consumer Electronics.


The P25-to-P75 spread — $158 to $1,091 — is the widest in the dataset at 6.9×, just ahead of Business & Industrial (6.6×). That spread reflects the enormous range of what “consumer electronics” actually means: a phone case merchant at the P25 and a high-end audio equipment retailer at the P75 are operating in completely different markets. The $479 median sits toward the lower end of that range, pulled down by the volume of smaller-ticket accessory and peripheral merchants in the cohort.


## AOV Trend — June 2025 through September 2026


The chart below tracks monthly median AOV for Consumer Electronics stores, with each month measured on its own (41–53 stores per month). With samples this size, single months can swing noticeably.


n=41–53 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Consumer Electronics.


The most dramatic movement in the trend came in fall 2025. After July–September ran at $287–$327, October 2025 jumped to $452 — a $165 increase in one month — and November held at $445. December dropped back to $317, and January–March 2026 ranged $292–$339, back near the summer 2025 lows.


The Oct–Nov 2025 spike is the most striking feature in the 16-month window. Consumer electronics purchases tend to increase in the pre-holiday period as buyers research and purchase gifts, upgrades, or seasonal deals — the timing is consistent with that kind of behavior, though the data alone doesn’t confirm the cause.


2026 has moved within a $292–$415 range. April ($405) and September ($415) were the high points, with May through August settling at $324–$354. On a matched same-store basis, AOV slipped 4.4% from Q2 to Q3 ($403 to $386), giving back part of the +14.4% gain the category posted from Q1 to Q2.


On a matched same-store basis (n=34 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV moved from $360 to $348 — a −3.2% year-over-year change. Note: the matched cohort for Consumer Electronics is the smallest in the dataset; treat this figure as directionally informative rather than statistically definitive.


## What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together


Consumer Electronics in 2026 has been defined by sharp swings between CVR and AOV. In Q2, the category posted the steepest quarterly CVR decline in the dataset while the customers who converted spent more than in any prior period. In Q3, both moves reversed: CVR rose more than in any other category, and same-store AOV fell further than in any other.


This kind of back-and-forth can reflect several things. Q2’s pattern — fewer conversions, higher order values — may have reflected lower-intent shoppers bouncing before checkout, or promotional pricing on lower-ticket items fading while higher-ticket items held demand. Q3’s reversal may reflect that mix shifting back, or simply the volatility of a small cohort. All of these are plausible. None is confirmed by the aggregate data alone.


For Consumer Electronics merchants, the bounce rate trend is the most concrete signal. A roughly 7-point bounce rate increase since April 2026, holding through Q3, is the kind of shift that shows up in revenue before it shows up clearly in attribution reports. If your CVR softened this year, the entry experience and page performance are worth examining closely.


> ***Consumer Electronics is a category where the AOV range ($158–$1,091) means the benchmark median ($479) may not describe your store at all. Whether your CVR is high or low relative to 1.39% is less meaningful without knowing where your AOV sits in that spread — and what your buyer’s research cycle looks like.***


## **A Note on Sub-Markets Within Consumer Electronics**


The 6.9× spread from P25 ($158) to P75 ($1,091) is the widest of any category in the 2026 year-to-date dataset — and it matters more here than in almost any other industry. Unlike a category like Health & Wellness, where most merchants operate at similar price points, Consumer Electronics is not one market. It’s several, stacked inside a single label.


At the low end — closer to the P25 — are merchants selling accessories, cables, cases, and peripherals. These stores typically see higher purchase frequency and lower per-order revenue. Their CVR profile may look more like a repeat-purchase category than the headline CE median suggests. At the high end — closer to the P75 and above — are merchants selling premium audio equipment, professional gear, or high-ticket consumer devices. Those stores likely convert at rates well below 1.39% and carry AOVs that pull the upper quartile to $1,091 and beyond.


The $479 median sits between these two worlds. For many CE merchants, it’s the wrong benchmark — not because the data is wrong, but because the sub-market you’re in shapes both what’s achievable in CVR and what’s normal in AOV. A merchant selling $80 phone cases and converting at 2.5% is performing well for their sub-market. A merchant selling $1,200 home theater systems and converting at 0.8% may also be performing well for theirs.


> ***Before benchmarking against the $479 median AOV or the 1.39% CVR, identify where your store sits in the $158–$1,091 range. The sub-market you’re in is a better reference point than the category aggregate. If your AOV is above $700, compare your CVR against considered-purchase benchmarks — not the CE headline.***
